controls.verification: Every workflow job declares least-privilege permissions; write scopes exist only on publishing, release, or attestation jobs.
Trusted collaborator inputs are passed through environment variables or strict version checks; unsafe shell interpolation is a test failure.
All release assets share the package version and source commit in release-metadata.json and are listed in SHA256SUMS.
SECURITY and supply-chain documentation define secret storage, token use, OIDC preference, exposure handling, and rotation.
Consumer verification commands cover checksums, Build provenance, VSA, and SBOM subjects.
Docs identify the expected GitHub OIDC workflow identity and the VSA verifier identity used by releases.
SUPPORT states the supported release line, support scope, and absence of a fixed SLA.
SUPPORT and SECURITY define when superseded releases stop receiving security updates.
MAINTAINERS defines that elevated access requires identity and need review; GitHub settings remain the external enforcement point.
Each npm and GitHub Packages release artifact ships with CycloneDX and SPDX SBOMs.
Releases are produced from one canonical repository; Gitee is a mirror and does not participate in release assembly.
controls.gap: The control applies only when a release composes multiple source repositories.

controls.verification: CONTRIBUTING lists supported platforms, toolchains, local commands, CI triggers, sharding, and release-only checks.
CONTRIBUTING requires a failing regression test for fixes and test updates for every behavior change.
The main ruleset requests non-author approval, but the repository currently has only one human maintainer.
controls.gap: A genuine second human reviewer is unavailable; the owner must not fake an approval with a bot or second identity.

controls.verification: The machine-readable threat model covers assets, actors, trust boundaries, STRIDE classes, attack paths, controls, and residual risk.
OpenVEX is generated from vulnerability dispositions and validated before release.
SECURITY defines Critical, High, Medium, and license remediation thresholds and release blocking.
License violations block release unless an explicit compatible exception is recorded.
Release candidates require dependency audit, dependency review, SBOM, and disposition checks.
PR dependency review blocks high severity dependency regressions and weekly audits cover pinned tooling and Rust locks.
SECURITY defines SAST severity thresholds and release blocking for actionable High or Critical findings.
CodeQL and the SAST ratchet run on pull requests and scheduled or push scans.
